$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the v3.2.4 migration. Edit this file, then run `node build-canary.mjs` to regenerate canary.html AND the step table inside MIGRATION-PLAN.md. Do not hand-edit either of those two files.
title: Xtrata v3.2.4 migration

steps.title: Register the candidate in the Clarinet project
steps.why: The candidate lives in contracts/drafts/v3.2.4/ and is not in the active plan. It must be registered to be checked or tested.
steps.action: Copy xtrata-v3.2.4-candidate.clar into contracts/clarinet/contracts/ and append a [contracts.xtrata-v3-2-4] entry with clarity_version = 3 and epoch = 'latest'. The epoch matters: epoch = 3.1 schedules it ahead of its own dependencies and clarinet fails with NoSuchContract.
steps.verify: clarinet check runs without a NoSuchContract error.
steps.rollback: Remove the entry and the copied file.

steps.title: Swap the NFT trait to the local one for checking
steps.why: The deployable file references the MAINNET nft-trait principal. Clarinet cannot resolve it and reports 'use of unresolved contract'.
steps.action: In the Clarinet copy only, uncomment the [LOCAL / CLARINET] impl-trait and use-trait lines and comment out the [MAINNET] pair. Never commit this swap back into the deployable file.
steps.verify: clarinet check reports all contracts checked with no errors.

steps.title: Run both contract test suites
steps.why: Proves the recipient split works and that nothing in v3.2.3 behaviour changed.
steps.action: From contracts/clarinet: `node xtrata-v3.2.4-draft.core.test.mjs` and `node xtrata-v3.2.4-sponsored.test.mjs`. Both suites unpause the core first, since cores deploy paused and everything else returns ERR-PAUSED (u109).
steps.verify: Core suite 18 passed / 0 failed. Sponsored suite 11 passed / 0 failed.
steps.rollback: None. Do not proceed on any failure.

steps.title: Decide the campaign-drops question
steps.why: This is the only decision that changes the size of the whole migration, so make it before anything touches a chain.
steps.action: xtrata-drops-v1-2 has exactly one hardcoded call to the core, at line 574 inside create-campaign-drop. Standard drops, claims and cancels all take an <nft-trait> parameter and work with 3.2.4 after an allow-list call. Decide now whether campaign drops must support 3.2.4 tokens. If yes, drops needs a redeploy (step S4). If no, the migration is admin calls only.
steps.verify: Decision recorded in this file under decisions.campaignDrops.

steps.title: Deploy the core to testnet
steps.why: Rehearse the deploy shape before spending mainnet STX on a 1600-line contract.
steps.action: Activate the [TESTNET] trait pair in the deployable file. Deploy as xtrata-v3-2-4 with Clarity 3 via the SDK. Do not deploy from a wallet UI: the wallet forces Clarity 4, under which `as-contract` in the migration path does not resolve.
steps.verify: The contract interface is retrievable from the testnet API.
steps.rollback: Redeploy under a new name. Testnet deploys are cheap and non-destructive.

steps.title: Set testnet fee units to the mainnet values
steps.why: Rehearsing against default fees would not exercise the real numbers, and the fee-change guards bound each move.
steps.action: Call set-single-tx-fee-unit, set-upload-chunk-fee-unit, set-begin-fee-unit, set-seal-fee-unit and set-upload-batch-fee-unit to the values in feeTargets. Each update is bounded: a new fee must be at most double and at least a tenth of the current one, so large moves need several calls.
steps.verify: quote-single-tx-fee(u16384, u1) returns single-tx-fee u11000.
steps.rollback: Set them back. Bounded either way.

steps.title: Unpause and run the mint flows on testnet
steps.why: End-to-end proof on a real chain rather than simnet.
steps.action: set-paused false, then run: a plain mint-single-tx, a sponsored mint-single-tx-to with a second wallet as recipient, and a staged begin / add-chunk-batch / seal cycle.
steps.verify: The sponsored mint leaves the recipient owning the token with a zero STX balance change, and the payer charged 11000 microSTX.

steps.title: Point a staging build at the testnet core and mint through the app
steps.why: The contract being right is not the same as the app driving it correctly. This is exactly what was missed when the fee post-condition regression shipped.
steps.action: Add a testnet registry entry, build, and inscribe through the real UI. Watch the post-conditions on the signing screen: they must be less-than-or-equal, and the capped amount must match quote-single-tx-fee.
steps.verify: A file inscribes from the UI, and the signing screen shows a LessEqual condition at the quoted fee, not an exact match.

steps.title: Deploy the core to mainnet
steps.why: The point of the exercise.
steps.action: Activate the [MAINNET] trait pair. Deploy as xtrata-v3-2-4 from the deployer at m/44'/5757'/3'/0/0, pinned to Clarity 3 via the SDK. Budget roughly 0.5 STX. The contract deploys PAUSED, which is the safety property this plan depends on: it exists but cannot be used until step C3.
steps.verify: The contract interface is retrievable and is-paused returns true.
steps.rollback: None. A deployed contract is permanent. It stays paused and unused, and you deploy 3.2.5 instead.

steps.title: Verify the deployed interface before touching anything else
steps.why: Catches a wrong-file or wrong-Clarity-version deploy while the contract is still paused and harmless.
steps.action: Fetch the contract interface and confirm mint-single-tx-to, mint-single-tx-recursive-to, mint-single-tx-with-relationships-to and migrate-from-v3-2-3 are all present, and that MAX-TOTAL-CHUNKS behaviour matches 128 MiB.
steps.verify: All four functions appear in the interface.

steps.title: Set the mainnet fee units
steps.why: A new core starts on defaults, which are far above the live values. Minting at default fees would overcharge every user.
steps.action: Set the five fee units to the feeTargets values. Remember the doubling and tenth bounds, so stepping down from the u100000 default to u10000 takes two calls.
steps.verify: quote-single-tx-fee(u16384, u1) returns single-tx-fee u11000 and total-fee u11000.
steps.rollback: Adjust again. Bounded, so no single call can do damage.

steps.title: Read the current next-id from v3.2.3
steps.why: Token id continuity. Without this, 3.2.4 starts at zero and you get two different inscriptions sharing an id across the two contracts, which is unresolvable afterwards.
steps.action: Call get-next-token-id on xtrata-v3-2-3 and write the number down. Do this as close to the cutover as possible, because every mint on 3.2.3 moves it.
steps.verify: You have the number.

steps.title: Pause v3.2.3
steps.why: Freezes next-id so the number from C1 cannot drift between reading it and setting it. Transfers are explicitly NOT paused, so the market, drops and migration all keep working.
steps.action: Call set-paused true on xtrata-v3-2-3.
steps.verify: is-paused on v3.2.3 returns true, and a transfer of an existing token still succeeds.

steps.title: Set next-id on v3.2.4 and unpause it
steps.why: This is the actual cutover moment. Do the id first, then the unpause, never the other way around.
steps.action: Call set-next-id on xtrata-v3-2-4 with the value from C1, confirm it, then call set-paused false.
steps.verify: get-next-token-id on 3.2.4 matches C1, and a real mint produces the next id in sequence with no collision against 3.2.3.
steps.rollback: set-paused true on 3.2.4, set-paused false on 3.2.3. Reversible until the first 3.2.4 mint lands.

steps.title: Allow-list 3.2.4 on the three sponsored markets
steps.why: No redeploy needed. In all three sponsored markets PRIMARY-NFT-CONTRACT is only read by the get-nft-contract getter. Enforcement runs off the AllowedNftContracts map.
steps.action: Call set-nft-allowed(<3.2.4 principal>, true) on xtrata-market-sponsored-stx-v1-1, xtrata-market-sponsored-sbtc-v1-1 and xtrata-market-sponsored-usdcx-v1-1.
steps.verify: is-nft-allowed returns true for 3.2.4 on each, and a 3.2.4 token can be listed and bought.

steps.title: Allow-list 3.2.4 on drops
steps.why: Enables standard drops for 3.2.4 tokens. create-drop, claim and cancel all take an <nft-trait> parameter, so they need no code change.
steps.action: Call set-nft-allowed(<3.2.4 principal>, true) on xtrata-drops-v1-2.
steps.verify: A 3.2.4 token can be dropped and claimed end to end.

steps.title: Confirm the no-change contracts really need no change
steps.why: Cheap to verify, expensive to assume.
steps.action: The non-sponsored markets take an <nft-trait> parameter and never name the core. xtrata-collection-mint-v1-4, xtrata-preinscribed-collection-sale-v1-0, xtrata-commerce and xtrata-vault contain no reference to the core at all. Spot check one market listing and one collection mint against 3.2.4.
steps.verify: Both succeed with no admin action taken.

steps.title: Redeploy drops for campaign support (ONLY if P4 said yes)
steps.why: create-campaign-drop hardcodes the 3.2.3 principal at line 574 and Clarity is immutable, so campaign drops cannot be extended by an admin call.
steps.action: Deploy xtrata-drops-v1-3 with the core reference updated, migrate the registry entry per the newest-contract-only rule, and leave v1-2 in place for existing campaigns.
steps.verify: A campaign drop can be created against a 3.2.4 token.
steps.rollback: Keep pointing the app at v1-2. The new contract sits unused.

steps.title: Redeploy the gateway
steps.why: xtrata-v3-2-3-gateway makes three hardcoded calls to the core and is named after it. It cannot be repointed.
steps.action: Deploy xtrata-v3-2-4-gateway with the core reference updated. Check what actually consumes the gateway before assuming it is needed at all.
steps.verify: Whatever depends on the gateway still resolves.
steps.rollback: Leave the old gateway serving 3.2.3 tokens.

steps.title: Add the 3.2.4 capabilities entry
steps.why: src/lib/contract/capabilities.ts is keyed by version string. An unknown version has no capability record and the mint route cannot be resolved.
steps.action: Add a '3.2.4' entry copying '3.2.3', with supportsNativeSingleTx true. Add a supportsSponsoredMint flag set true for 3.2.4 and false everywhere else, so the UI can show the pay-for-someone-else option only where it exists.
steps.verify: The app resolves capabilities for 3.2.4 without falling through to a default.

steps.title: Swap the registry entry, do not append
steps.why: House rule: the app uses only the newest version of a contract. A registry listing two versions of the same contract is a bug, not a compatibility feature. The /drops page previously burned 34 wasted read-only calls per load this way.
steps.action: In src/config/public.ts, change PUBLIC_CONTRACT to xtrata-v3-2-4 and set legacyContractId to the 3.2.3 id so the viewer keeps resolving older inscriptions.
steps.verify: A 3.2.3 inscription still renders in the viewer, and new mints go to 3.2.4.
steps.rollback: Point the registry back at 3.2.3. The app is the only thing that moves.

steps.title: Fix the fee model before shipping the pivot
steps.why: src/lib/contract/fees.ts still models a single fee-unit and returns 300000 for a single-tx mint that actually costs 11000. Shipping the pivot without this carries a known 27x over-estimate into the new core.
steps.action: Replace estimateContractFees for v3+ with the on-chain quote-single-tx-fee and quote-staged-fee calls that already exist on the client. Confirm no mint path emits FungibleConditionCode.Equal.
steps.verify: A mint's signing screen caps at the quoted fee with LessEqual.

steps.title: Triage the remaining 3.2.3 references in source
steps.why: Roughly twenty files name 3.2.3. Most legitimately record where past on-chain activity happened and must NOT be rewritten, or the record becomes false.
steps.action: Leave historical records alone (src/lib/drops/collection-lock.ts, src/sponsor-ops.ts float tracking, the handover files). Update anything that resolves the CURRENT core. Retire historical references only when the underlying activity finishes.
steps.verify: Full app test suite passes.

steps.title: Inscribe through the live app and check the fee actually charged
steps.why: The last regression was invisible in code review and obvious in a transaction.
steps.action: Inscribe a small file through the production UI. Read the resulting transaction: confirm one STX transfer of 11000 microSTX, a LessEqual post-condition, and tx_status success.
steps.verify: Transfer is 11000 microSTX and the post-condition is not an exact match.

steps.title: Run one sponsored mint in anger
steps.why: The feature this whole deploy exists for.
steps.action: From a funded wallet, mint-single-tx-to a wallet holding zero STX. Confirm the recipient owns the token, is recorded as creator, and was charged nothing.
steps.verify: Recipient owns and is creator. Recipient STX balance unchanged.

steps.title: Watch for post-condition aborts for 48 hours
steps.why: abort_by_post_condition is the failure mode that costs users money while looking like nothing happened. It will not page anyone.
steps.action: Poll the 3.2.4 contract transaction list and alert on any abort_by_post_condition. Check for sent_equal_to conditions specifically, which should never appear.
steps.verify: Zero post-condition aborts.
steps.rollback: Pause 3.2.4 and repoint the app at 3.2.3.
